- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 1.0) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -1.5), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–4% to counteract downward bias.
- Model consistently underestimates prices after recent spikes (e.g., >70) — add 2–5% buffer for 3–7 day horizon.
- Forecast mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is 2–3% above recent 18d average, reduce by 1–2% to align with historical mean reversion.
- For 30d horizon, if sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings, model tends to lag — add 1–3% to forecast to capture momentum.
- If sentiment is neutral or volatile (±0.5), model often overfits short-term noise — use 3–5 day smoothing or drop extreme outliers in forecast tail.
